quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson

quotes.social_post: Richard Jefferson says Victor Wembanyama is so unique that you literally cannot create a player like him in NBA 2K because it would be unrealistic

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye on James Harden's evolution into a distributor for the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: He's not the old MVP James Harden. He's a distributor, right? It's Donovan Mitchell's team.
quotes.quote: James Harden, I think definitely with that team, it's just like he's such a point guard at heart to me. He's not the old MVP James Harden. He's a distributor, right? It's Donovan Mitchell's team. But for him to have an outburst like that, just reminding people, I think everyone talks about some of the best shooters in the game and they don't mention James Harden, but he's changed the game in so many ways when it comes to like getting to the free throw line or step-back jumpers, it's just his imagination.
quotes.social_post: Channing Frye on James Harden: He is not the old MVP version anymore, he is a pure distributor at heart who has changed the game with his imagination

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic's elite performance against Chicago
quotes.excerpt: I think the one that stands out to me is Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic.
quotes.quote: I think the one that stands out to me is Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic. One, these dudes have been playing outstanding. They've been playing out, but my issue is, it takes that much from them to beat Chicago in overtime, right? And Chicago, and that's the thing. This team, when they were playing, when they were kind of in the beginning, they were doing what they were doing, they hadn't had a signature win. That win against who did they just play? Houston and then Boston. So they had back-to-back wins. My point is, these guys are, like Jamal Murray was All-NBA last year, he's playing even better this year. Jokic, still playing at an MVP level.
quotes.social_post: Richard Jefferson on the Nuggets: Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic are playing at an elite level, but it is concerning that it takes that much effort for them to beat teams like Chicago

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins on Christian Braun's need to step up for the Nuggets
quotes.excerpt: They're waiting on him to take that leap.
quotes.quote: The guys that they pay, the others, right? The others, Christian Braun. They're waiting on him to take that leap. By the way, he defensively, he's elite. He's great. Offensively, he needs the three ball. Yeah, but he has to even be better defensively because we know that they don't have a rim protector. Like he needs to be somewhat playing at an all-NBA, all-defensive second team type level for them to take that, seriously.
quotes.social_post: Kendrick Perkins says Christian Braun needs to play at an All-Defensive second team level for the Nuggets to be serious contenders since they lack a rim protector

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins on Aaron Gordon's need to play like an All-Star
quotes.excerpt: They got to find a way to get Aaron Gordon back to playing like the All-Star Aaron Gordon.
quotes.quote: They got to find a way to get Aaron Gordon back to playing like the All-Star Aaron Gordon. And when I'm saying that is because sometimes it's not all about what he's doing for us like on the floor, it's the passion. And I can only think about the shit he been going through for the last two years dealing with the same hamstring injury, right? And then he had, you know, death in the family with his brother. It's a lot to overcome, but it seemed like, because he's the most important piece. Like when you think about, think about what he was doing when they actually won the championship, he was balling. He was unreal.
quotes.social_post: Kendrick Perkins on Aaron Gordon: He is the most important piece for Denver and they need to get him back to playing with the passion and level he had during their championship run

quotes.speaker: Davion Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Davion Mitchell on finding balance between being passive and aggressive
quotes.excerpt: It's a balance for me of being passive and active, you know what I mean?
quotes.quote: It's a balance for me of being passive and active, you know what I mean? So I got to be a little bit more active. That's when we're at our best. And I'm taking pressure off of everybody else, but this is a great team win.
quotes.social_post: Davion Mitchell on his role: It is a constant balance for me between being passive and active, but we are at our best when I am being aggressive

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the importance of the power forward position for Nikola Jokic's success
quotes.excerpt: Every star player has a formula. When they found it, it was first Paul Millsap.
quotes.quote: Every star player has a formula. When they found it, it was first Paul Millsap. When Paul Millsap went there and you had a do-it-all power forward, Jokic really blossomed. And then it went Jeremy Grant. Remember Jeremy Grant had that great year? I think Jeremy Grant was on their team in the bubble. They go to the conference finals. Jeremy Grant gets paid a lot of money, and then they go get then they go get Aaron Gordon. And you see the formula. So that athletic, do-it-all, versatile, defensive power forward, which Aaron Gordon was, Paul Millsap was, and Jeremy Grant was. All three of them have the formula. And so when if Aaron, being to his point, Aaron is the key. So if Aaron is not that best version of Aaron, that really hurts them because he is the key piece. It's always been the key piece, the same way Shaq needed Penny, Kobe, and D-Wade. He needed that ultra, ultra elite scorer next to him. That was Shaq's key. For Jokic, that key is the power forward position.
quotes.social_post: Richard Jefferson breaks down the Nuggets formula: For Nikola Jokic to succeed, he needs that versatile, athletic power forward archetype like Paul Millsap, Jerami Grant, or Aaron Gordon

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins on Victor Wembanyama's MVP aspirations and performance
quotes.excerpt: He's watching the league and he actually wants to win the MVP.
quotes.quote: One is that with Wemby, he's watching the league. So he's watching the league and the other thing is that he actually wants to win the MVP. He wants to win the MVP. He's been on record saying it, but I think and he should, and why I say that is because when you're watching, you say, oh, look at him trying to get his numbers. But let me tell Wemby, let me tell you something, before you was even born, before we were born, stat padding has been around.
quotes.social_post: Kendrick Perkins on Victor Wembanyama: He is chasing the MVP and watching the league closely, but he should not worry about the stat padding narrative because that has always existed

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins on why Karl-Anthony Towns is an underrated offensive player
quotes.excerpt: None of that stat line has impressed me more than Karl-Anthony Towns' 30 and 13.
quotes.quote: None of that stat line has impressed me more than Karl-Anthony Towns' 30 and 13. It's not, I'm going to say this. Let me explain why, because he's still sacrificing. There's not one big man in the league, including Wemby, that I'm fucking taking over Karl-Anthony Towns offensively. Offensively. If you want to, what? He giving you everything.
quotes.social_post: Kendrick Perkins: There is not one big man in the league, including Wemby, that I am taking over Karl-Anthony Towns offensively right now

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins on Bam Adebayo's growth and fit with Giannis Antetokounmpo
quotes.excerpt: I think he was worried about pleasing Giannis so much when Giannis first like, hey big dog, get comfortable.
quotes.quote: To me, I mean what Bron said last year to Luka, don't fit in, fit out. I think he was worried about pleasing Giannis so much when Giannis first like, hey big dog, get comfortable. That he wasn't being aggressive. The Bam I saw against Tyler Herro and what we been seeing of late, it's like, bro, get into your bag. Because everybody I talked to from the Heat, whether that's UD on our phone conversations or Jimmy Butler, they like, nah, Perk, like Bam got that shit. Everybody tell me, they like, Bam got it. It's just, it's like, hey bro, consistently go out there and have that, that, I'm him mentality.
quotes.social_post: Kendrick Perkins on Bam Adebayo: Everyone around the Heat tells me Bam has that dog in him, he just needs to consistently play with that I am him mentality

quotes.speaker: Davion Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Davion Mitchell explains the origin of his 'Off Night' nickname
quotes.excerpt: They kind of came with the name Off Night, which is me guarding like the top guards.
quotes.quote: Shout out to three of my closest friends, they was GAs with me at Baylor, Rim, Peyton, and Matt Gray. They all on different, I think Rim's at Texas Tech and I think Peyton is now, I forgot what school he is, but he's a coach there and Matt Gray is working with the G-League in Denver and they kind of came with the name Off Night, which is me guarding like the top guards in our league, and they wasn't having the their usual nights that they have every day. And I was just in the film room with them, we were just chatting and he was like, yo, we going to call you Off Night. And it just ran with it and it's kind of crazy that that simple little conversation made the nickname into now in the NBA and everyone knows it.
quotes.social_post: Davion Mitchell explains the origin of his Off Night nickname: It came from a conversation with college friends about how I make top guards have bad nights

quotes.speaker: Davion Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Davion Mitchell on his defensive approach against top NBA guards
quotes.excerpt: I don't look at one person, oh, I got to turn up even more because I'm playing this person.
quotes.quote: I don't look at one person, oh, I got to turn up even more because I'm playing this person. Because I know who I am and I know that I bring the same amount of energy each game. And I think that whatever is needed for us to win, I'm going to do. And it's not like, oh, I got to outplay this person, whatever it takes to win, that's what I'm going to do.
quotes.social_post: Davion Mitchell on his defensive mindset: I do not change my approach based on who I am guarding, I just bring the same energy and do whatever it takes to win

quotes.speaker: Davion Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Davion Mitchell on his defensive development and learning from Jrue Holiday
quotes.excerpt: I remember that we played them last year and I would probably say Jrue Holiday.
quotes.quote: I remember that we played them last year and I would probably say Jrue Holiday. He's like one of those guys where it's like, when I was bringing the ball up, because usually I don't have a problem bringing the ball up, I'm like, all right, this dude ain't about to put pressure on me. I'm going to just run by him, I'm faster than him. But with Jrue, like he's like, he's such a smart defender, it's like, I don't even know how to explain it. He like jump into the move before I am even thinking about it. It's like, to the point where I'm like, bro, let me get off, I never been a guy like, let me get off this.
quotes.social_post: Davion Mitchell on Jrue Holiday: He is such a smart defender that he jumps into my moves before I even think about them

quotes.speaker: Davion Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Davion Mitchell on how he learned defensive techniques from Jrue Holiday
quotes.excerpt: I actually took that from Jrue Holiday that Perk said that. Like this summer, I was like.
quotes.quote: I actually took that from Jrue Holiday that Perk said that. Like this summer, I was like, I got the rookies, I brought the rookies to the the gym. Obviously I was like, y'all come to the gym regardless. And okay, if y'all tired, no, y'all come to the gym this summer and I literally was like, I'm going to, I'm literally just going to guard. I didn't do no offense that day. I did offense in the morning and I'm like, yo, I'm just going to guard in the evening. And I just guarded them. Obviously Ryan Arcidiacono and Trey and them dudes are nice, so it was kind of a little bit difficult, but it was just fun. And I kind of took that from Jrue Holiday, um, just because I seen that video too when he just getting stops. And I was like, yo, I want to try this out and I loved it.
quotes.social_post: Davion Mitchell says he spent his summer just guarding players in the gym to emulate the defensive intensity he saw from Jrue Holiday

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the importance of veteran leadership for young players
quotes.excerpt: A lot of times when guys fresh come out of college, their games aren't polished.
quotes.quote: I know you started with our boy Luke Walton, friend of the program, over at Sac, right? And then you got to a place, and people don't understand, a lot of times when guys fresh come out of college, their games aren't polished. You are now in a space where offensively, this looks like who you are. You look very comfortable in this role. And once players figure it out, there's no going back. There's no going back.
quotes.social_post: Richard Jefferson on young players: Once a player finds their role and gets comfortable in the NBA, there is no going back

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson

quotes.quote: Is it harder to average 26 officially with guys around you that with Tyrese Maxey team, or is it harder to average 26 in the position that Cade is in?
